passes.summary: Fourth straight down day (S&P 500 -1.0% to a five-month low, VIX 25.5) into Nvidia's report, which beat and raised; futures up about half a percent tonight. Two takes where the story itself changed today: short Nike after an investor day that pushed the recovery out a year, and long Nvidia against chips after the first clean print since Huang left. The rest of the screen is stretches with no dated reason to turn, breakdowns in things already washed out on the night the AI trade got relief, or binary events inside the week (Dish mediation and the UK ruling on McCormick tomorrow, Gap's report Thursday).

Nvidia's beat failed to hold (it and the chip ETF turned red inside 20 minutes) and the S&P is slipping toward a fifth loss with VIX near 24.6; the money is moving on the Fed (Waller asking for a half-point hike, minutes at 1:00 PM CT) through a metals liquidation (copper -5%, gold -2.5% to a one-year low) and on two retail prints that beat on traffic. Takes: Target and TJX long against the retail ETF, gold miners short outright; the stretched bounces have no turn and the index shorts no story of their own.

Flat index hiding a violent rotation: a Fed hike on Dec 9 is nearly fully priced (10-year 5.05%), gold, copper and oil are all down 3-5%, insurers are down 9-10% on the CMS audit rule, retail and cybersecurity are up. Three takes where a name has its own fresh story (DIS re-rating, SQM's miss and price warning, refiners' margin collapse); the rest are macro beta the book already holds or has no edge in.

More than twenty brokers cut targets and about ten went to Hold in the nine days before the report; they now have a beat-and-raise to write up. The legal overhang is unchanged, and that is what the remaining discount is for.

reasoning.case_against: Nvidia fell the day after three of its last four beats; a 3-5% gain is small for a beat this size, which says sellers are waiting at 163-168; the margin guide is three points lower; $118B of guarantees, $32B of neocloud commitments and four customers at 47% of sales are what the SEC story is about; and the headlines with no date (SEC, DOJ on Megaspeed, a late 10-Q, the Commerce rule) all cut one way.
